annotations.text:
What changes if fertiliser is always in the water

• Data: nothing new. Every watering is stored with fertilized: true, so the history stays true if the habit ever stops.
• Care: the Last fertilised row goes — it would always say the same as Last watered.
• History: “with fertiliser” disappears from every row; it would be on all of them.
• Same-day fold: pressing water after fertiliser no longer means anything, so that half of the rule goes quiet.
• Log sheet and split button lose their Fertiliser option.
A · Smallest change. Still two taps, as decided. But a fan of two is half an arc — the question is whether it still needs to fan at all.
B · Drop waters on tap; the ink chip beside it opens the sheet. One tap, like you asked. Cost: it undoes the deliberate two taps, and a mis-tap means swiping the row away (no undo).
C · Hold ~0.5 s and the ring fills, then it pours. A plain tap opens the sheet. One motion, still deliberate. Cost: a hidden gesture — needs the hint the first few times.
D · Water lives next to the fact it changes; the corner button is just “log”. Cost: only on the Care tab, and mid-screen instead of under the thumb.
Log sheet · With Fertiliser gone, Watering is a group of one. Left keeps it anyway; right folds Water in with Repot as things you did.
Settings · One switch, collection-wide. Per plant would be possible, but you described a habit, not a plant.
Desktop · A split button with one item behind its caret is a menu for nothing. Two plain buttons instead: Water, and Log activity.
1 · As built. Quiet and out of the way — too far out of the way: it reads as a menu for the plant, not as the second thing you do here.
2 · A 48 px + right above the drop, in the same thumb reach. Water stays biggest and closest to the corner. Cost: two floating buttons over the record.
3 · One bar over the tab bar: Log activity written out, the drop at its end. The most obvious of the six. Cost: the widest thing floating over the page.
4 · “+ Log” as a real button on the name’s row. Visible the moment the page opens. Cost: top of the screen, out of thumb reach.
5 · New. On a plant page the tab bar’s centre button logs to this plant (ink, “Log”); everywhere else it stays New plant. No new button at all. Cost: the same place meaning two things.
6 · New. The log’s own circles sit on the Care tab, one tap straight into the right entry. Cost: only on Care, and it makes that tab busier.

Where Log activity lives on a phone

Water is first: the drop stays where it is, the biggest thing under the thumb. Log is second — it should be findable without hunting, but never compete with the drop.

A + 2, with the date

One sheet: the date on top, the camera under it, the grid under that.

• Without a photo it works exactly as now: tap a circle and it is logged on the chosen day.
• With a photo, the same circles log that entry with the photo attached, and a sixth circle, Photo only, appears in the spot the old Photo button had.
• The date sits first because it applies to everything below it, photo included.

The Add a photo chip and the Photo circle both go: the camera tile replaces them.

Open questions
• A photo taken today but logged for 12 Sept: file it on the picked day (as drawn), or keep the photo’s own date?
• Should the photo from a New leaf or Blooming also become the plant’s photo, the way a photograph already does?

A · The sheet opens on the camera

The … opens a sheet whose first question is a photo; the other things sit underneath as small chips. After the shutter you tag what the photo shows and log it.

For: one place for everything, closest to what you have.
Against: five steps for a new leaf, and a Note now sits behind “Nothing to photograph?”.

B · Straight from the hero

The “Photograph this plant” pill already sits on the photograph. It goes to the camera, then a full-screen review where you say what it shows and whether it becomes the plant’s photo.

For: the photo lands where photos live; no … needed.
Against: once a plant has a photo the pill is gone, so it needs another home on the hero.

C · Log first, ask after

The shutter logs a Photo entry straight away. A card offers New leaf, Blooming, Repot; tap one and the same row becomes that entry with the photo. Ignore it and it stays a photo.

For: fewest taps; nothing is lost if you walk away.
Against: a card that asks something after the fact, every time.

D · The grid you now have, with a photo slot

The shipped grid, minus its Photo circle: the “Add a photo” chip grows into a slot on top. Take one, and any circle logs that entry with it; “Just the photo” logs it bare.

For: smallest step from what is built; photo stays optional.
Against: the photo is still a detour rather than the lead.

Log activity, round two

Water is one press on the drop now, so the sheet is for everything else. Water stays reachable for one reason: the day you forgot to log it.

The three I made in the app’s own language come first. The last two are new ideas.
1 · The sheet you have, with the plant first and Water turned into one quiet row at the foot: “Watered on another day”. Cost: still three groups to scan.
2 · Six circles, no labels over them, in the order you reach for them. Half the height. Cost: loses the did / the plant did / written-down reading.
3 · Rows that say what each one will ask for — a repot asks three things, a new leaf asks nothing. Cost: taller, and less of a gesture than tapping a circle.

4 · New. You are usually stood in front of the plant because something happened. The camera opens first; you tag what the photo shows, and it logs as that entry with the picture. Cost: a note or a repot without a photo is one step further.

5 · New. Type or dictate one sentence; the sheet reads it back as entries before anything is logged, and you remove what it got wrong. The in-browser model the name dice already uses could do the reading. Cost: the most to build, and it has to be right often enough to trust.
